text: Ḥizb al-Baḥr now runs to the end: the practice opens with the Duʿāʾ al-Iʿtiṣām and closes with the Ikhtitām, as its title says, every line of the house of Names is in it, and the counts (×3, ×7) are set. The classical litanies, the Kunūz working book (all 64 entries, with the compiler's restrictions), the edition's phrase sheets and constructions, and page 81 of the Sharḥ are shown whole, exactly as printed. My day now has Kunūz's 175 places, the Karachi prayer method and its high-latitude rule. The Iḥyāʾ Engine and Kunūz al-Dhikr are retired: their daily runs are stopped and everything of value is here.

My day now holds your Journal: write down each working, dhikr, dream or study session and the engine stamps it for you with the planetary day and hour, the lunar mansion, the lunar day and the Hijri date. Type a Name and its value appears; forge its square from there. Search, filter by kind, add the outcome later (a list shows the workings still waiting for one), export, and import your journal from the Iḥyāʾ Engine. It follows you to every device, and every operation's page now has “Write it in the journal”. Also: al-Ḥuṣarī and al-Minshāwī now recite the whole Qurʾān in Read → Qurʾān beside Alafasy.

Read now holds the Qurʾān: tap Qurʾān on the shelf for all 114 sūras in the muṣḥaf's own text with Pickthall's and Yusuf Ali's English, transliteration, and the abjad of every āya. Open “tafsīr · the masters” under any āya for the nine commentaries the Iḥyāʾ carries — al-Jalālayn and Ibn Kathīr for the plain sense, al-Qushayrī, Ibn ʿAjība, Ismāʿīl Ḥaqqī, al-Najmiyya, al-Qāshānī, al-Sulamī and al-Tustarī for the inner — with “In English” and “Teach me this verse”. Mishary Alafasy recites the whole Qurʾān here now: the sūra, one āya or from where you are, repeated up to 100 times, slowly if you like, with the āya lit as he recites (al-Ḥuṣarī and al-Minshāwī come next). Find any verse by its number, its sūra or a word; ☆ marks follow you to your other devices; a verse number in Reference → Verses opens it here.

Learn now holds the Iḥyāʾ's Wird and the Ninety-nine: count any dhikr or any Name at its abjad on a big circle (Space or tap, a buzz at every 33, a soft bell at the round's end, a breath guide, counting by voice) and write it in your journal; learn the Ninety-nine as flash cards that come back when you are about to forget them; say a Name and see which letters were heard; and see your path — study minutes, dhikr, the Names, chapter by chapter — with al-Muʿallim's letter for the week (it writes itself on Fridays). A quick card on My day shows what is due. Your Wird record from the Iḥyāʾ Engine came with it.

Read now holds the Kunūz Maktaba: tap Kunūz · Maktaba for the channel's 24 books page by page — the Shādhilī aḥzāb, Ḥizb al-Wiqāya, Duʿāʾ Sayfī, Jāliyat al-Akdār, the seven Jaʿfariyya litanies, the Kashkūl-i Kalīmī, the Dhikr methods and more — with the English beside each page, a page strip, zoom, swipe or arrow keys, ☆ marks and your place in every book kept across your devices, and a search of every page. The Ḥizb al-Wiqāya edition and the Laṭāʾif codex now read right here. Library shows the channel's images (tap to enlarge), the reading list and every document named on DhikrNotes. The Ustādh now searches the books too.

Ask now has two teachers. Tap “The Ustādh” to ask the teacher of Kunūz al-Dhikr, as Kunūz has him: he searches the DhikrNotes posts, the awrād, the Sharḥ, Rev5, the practices and every sohbah before he answers, cites them, quizzes you one multiple-choice question at a time (tap A–D to answer), and reminds you that texts are not idhn. In both teachers’ answers, a cited post, sohbah, Sharḥ page, Iḥyāʾ page or operation now opens when you tap it, and each conversation is kept and follows you to your other devices. The “Ask” buttons in the awrād, Dīwān and sohbah readers now ask the Ustādh. Also fixed: Arabic typed into a sohbah’s find box now matches.

Learn now holds Kunūz al-Ḥalqa, the teaching circle of Kunūz al-Dhikr: 61 lessons in 8 tracks (the path's foundations, the Naqshbandī masters, the Dalāʾil, the Qādirī path, the Shādhilī aḥzāb, the Sharḥ of Ḥizb al-Baḥr, the sacred year, living sohbahs). The teacher picks the season's lesson or the next one, teaches it from the posts and awrād with references, and checks it with five multiple-choice questions (keys 1–4); missed questions come back in a review. Also: a timed study session, the syllabus, Recite with me line by line, the Ḥifẓ drill that hides words, and your progress. A lesson is prepared once and kept, and the day's lesson now appears in your Kunūz wird on My day.

Read now holds all 2,302 sohbahs of Mawlana Shaykh Nāẓim: tap Kunūz · Sohbahs. Find a title as you type, or press Enter to search every word of every talk (ranked as in Kunūz, with how often each word occurs and the passage). Each sohbah reads in paragraphs with find-in-text, larger or smaller type, your place kept, ☆ keep, recently read, the Qurʾān verses it names read from the muṣḥaf with their abjad, and Ask about this.

Read now holds the Kunūz Dīwān: all 1,240 posts of the DhikrNotes channel, newest first, with search that marks the words, topic chips, a year strip, ṭarīqa, “with text”, documents, and ☆ to keep a post. Open any post to read the Qurʾān it cites straight from the muṣḥaf (with its abjad), the abjad of its Arabic lines, earlier/later posts, and where the same text was posted again. Also fixed: Arabic written in Indo-Pak spelling (ی ک ہ) is now counted correctly in every abjad.

Read now holds the Kunūz awrād as books: tap Kunūz · Awrād at the top of Read for the Naqshbandī awrād with the whole Dalāʾil al-Khayrāt, the Qādirī awrād with al-Ṣalāt al-Kubrā, and the Shādhilī aḥzāb with Ḥizb al-Baḥr — every line in vowelled Arabic, transliteration and English, with a choice of Arabic typeface and size, the abjad of any line, ☆ marks, and a search that opens at the line. The Sharḥ of Ḥizb al-Baḥr and the Rev5 compilation read page by page. From your practices and the runner, “Open the text” brings you straight to the section.

My day now holds your Kunūz wird: each practice in its prayer slot with ticks that follow you across devices, a seven-day strip and streak, and ▶ Do it opens the guided runner — one step at a time with the Arabic, transliteration and English, the day's Dalāʾil ḥizb or Kubrā portion line by line, a bead to count each repetition, your place kept if you stop. Also here: Practices & the sacred year (every occasion of the Hijrī year, step by step) and the Tasbīḥ, which can now count any Name at its abjad. Your Kunūz record came with it.

The Read tab is now the whole Iḥyāʾ as a book: every chapter page by page with the Arabic as printed and every figure where the book puts it (each square re-checked), the chapter's sections, figures, numbered workings and corrections, bookmarks and highlights, sepia or paper pages, a search of the whole book that opens on the page, and how much of each chapter you have read.

The Study now runs inside the engine (Learn): the whole Iḥyāʾ in 855 lessons with the teacher — he chooses what you need (what you may have forgotten first, a chapter's map before you enter it, then the next pages, taught and checked with four answers), pauses for prayer, and keeps your progress from the Iḥyāʾ Engine. A course map shows every lesson, and each chapter has an exam with a record of reading when you pass.

al-Ḥalqa, the daily circle, now runs inside the engine (Learn): the day's verse and Name counted on screen, the square of the first hour built cell by cell, your ṭarīqa's wird, the day's portion of Yā-Sīn with its Qurʾān text, the lesson through the book (continuing at p.66 where the Iḥyāʾ left off), a multiple-choice review, the closing verse and the journal — and every planetary hour the next of the Ninety-nine. Hand it any Name or number and it builds and checks the square. No machine voice ever says the Arabic.

The Forge's "From a figure of the book" now holds all 414 open figures of the Iḥyāʾ, not only the squares: every talisman, seal, circle and table can be set as a plate in the archangels' frame with your own lines above and below and saved as an image; squares turn to the four elements or mirror, and any square can be set exactly as printed.

New in the Forge: the Ṭilasm Studio. Any of 422 talismans from the Iḥyāʾ and the Durūs lessons — rings, seals, the Basmala cross, the archangels' frame, the book's own figures drawn as clean line — composed whole for your Name, need or number, with its square rebuilt and checked, ready to download as SVG or PNG.
Six tabs instead of nine: My day, Learn, Read, Forge, Reference and Ask. Verses, squares, operations, materials and timing now live together under Reference.
New Read tab: the Iḥyāʾ text page by page with search across the whole book, and a search of Kunūz al-Dhikr.
Read-aloud in Ask no longer tries to pronounce Arabic: it skips Arabic words and leaves them on screen.
